doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Obsessing over a composition; episodic writing as puzzle
summary: The drums and bass are briefly debated, then she describes composing as problem solving, episodic and like a puzzle.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Na, the drums are supreme but they also don’t work without the bass so yeah.

If you’re in the middle of composing or arranging, do you become obsessed with it? And by that I mean you’re driving to Eastman or you’re taking a walk that you find that you’re working on this arrangement like all right what do I do next. It’s like trying to solve little problems in your head?

Yeah it’s the construction that goes on and you’re, again this interview I did before had a similar question and I was just like — he asked me, he said, “So do you ever dream about your compositions? Like do you have dreams about compositions or that you want to have?” And I was like you mean literally sleeping? I’m like when I sleep I sleep. Unfortunately I get caught up in something that I might be working in, that’s a drag because I can’t sleep because of that. But it’s not a drag because that means I’m really activated in solving — doing that problem solving you’re talking about. Because something has to come from the step I’ve stopped at. Or, it also might go in the garbage, who knows? But it’s sort of like I really get into it I do feel the power of the composition moving forward. And that comes also from preparation a little bit. So a lot of times I might try for, I mean another word I’m always using is a lot of my music is not programmatic necessarily but it’s full of different episodes, so it’s episodic. It’s quite a bit of episodic — I mean I can break some stuff down into a one minute lead sheet if I had to, but instead I’ve been adding episodes all around it. So those are little — I like to think of it as working on a puzzle. It’s really a puzzle for me.
Do you find that your music —

Well I have this little red piece and I don’t know where it goes yet but I’m going to have to build up around it to get that little red piece connecting. But then there another red piece spot too, I’m not sure which one I’ll get to — it kind of has to drive me as much as I drive it, which is different than problem solving necessarily.
